title: Playing at the fights between rounds
summary: Williams explains how the band advertised the fights and then played at the Coliseum and Hyman Park between rounds for six dollars a night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And then we used to, I had all them fights. We used to play all the fights. Oh, yeah? Yeah. How did that work? Oh, we used to advertise for the fight. Mm-hmm. Back on the same day. Mm-hmm.

Mm-hmm. It was for the Coliseum. And then after when we get through advertising for the fight, every time, we drive right on to the fight and bring the instruments there. Then at eight o'clock, we start playing again. Mm-hmm. Sometimes we get in at seven o'clock, seven thirty. This be time, just to rig up and start playing. We play in between the rounds.
Well, how long would that be? Could you play a little horse?
Well, they had, according to some of the fights they had. Mm-hmm. You see, you had your little amateur fights, you know?
Three rounds, four rounds. Three Lama deal.
Yeah, you know what I mean?

And then you had your main goal. Mm-hmm. Your main goal would be as practical as the last bout, you know? Mm-hmm. And we, sometime it'd be, it was the Hyman Park then, where the big motel, right? Mm-hmm. We used to be out there. Sometime, it'd be Wednesday nights and Friday nights. Friday nights probably used to be, it's a big night. And even sometime they'd put them fights off until on a Sunday. On a Sunday down and forth. And we had all that. And all that showed up. All that was my work.

And you had plenty of time then between the different fights, the three Lama's and the main bout and everything, so you could actually get some numbers in there. Yeah. You could actually just play one chorus. I see, I always wondered about it because I never saw a band.

And we would fight fans. Yeah. We would fight fans, we loved it. And we didn't get but six bucks. And I played over here at St. Philip and St. Claude, I played over there for a long time. And I had this girl Alma Money, Monday. Alma, she's across the lake now.
